Subject: Oct 31 webinar — primary stream (On24) and Zoom RTMP failover / recording consent

Hi Jasmine,

Quick note as we lock the run of show for Oct 31: AcmeCorp will be the presenting sponsor for the 11am PT session. We need confirmation on two items before we publish the registration page this week:

1) Streaming topology: AcmeCorp prefers On24 as the primary CDN, but wants Zoom as an RTMP failover if the ON24 feed drops. Can Redwood accept a dual-output setup (On24 primary, Zoom RTMP fallback) and confirm how the transition will look from attendee perspective?

2) Recording & consent: We need the registration flow to capture explicit consent for recording + sponsor usage (checkbox, link to terms) and also to confirm retention period and whether recordings will be stored in our KMS or Redwood-managed storage.

Attached is our standard sponsor SLA (acmecorp_sla.pdf) and a short list of requirements. Can you and your ops team confirm by EOD Wednesday?

Thanks,

Lara Chen
Events Manager, AcmeCorp

Subject: Re: Oct 31 webinar — primary stream (On24) and Zoom RTMP failover / recording consent

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear list. Short answers and an ops plan suggestion below.

1) Dual-output failover: Yes. Proposed flow:
- Primary: On24 ingest from Redwood encoder (we push a stable stream).
- On failure (lost keyframes / >3 consecutive I-frames missed) we switch program to Zoom RTMP endpoint within 10s. Zoom will be set to join the webinar as a broadcast-only participant to avoid attendee confusion.
- Attendee experience: most viewers will see a <5–15s gap and a short overlay message we control: "We're switching to backup stream — thanks for bearing with us."

Operational notes: we will run an end-to-end RTMP failover test the week prior (see attached checklist). We will also enable automatic clip recording on both platforms (redundant recording) for immediate recovery if needed. Attachment: stream_checklist.xlsx

2) Recording & consent: We can add a required checkbox on the Redwood registration form: "I consent to recording and to my likeness/content being used by AcmeCorp and Redwood Inference per the event terms." We will link to the SLA/terms on the form. Retention: default Redwood policy is 90 days for recordings in our hosted environment, but for sponsor materials we can retain up to 180 days if AcmeCorp signs the attached addendum. For KMS: Redwood-managed encryption keys are available; if you require customer-managed keys (BYOK) we need a separate onboarding ticket for Private deployments.

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm sponsor retention (90 vs 180 days) by Wednesday.
- Schedule failover test with On24 + Zoom for Tue Oct 27 10am PT (30m).
- Finalize registration copy with legal link and consent checkbox — I can send draft text today.

I attached the test checklist so ops can comment.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Field Marketing Ops, Redwood Inference
